title: Summed key counts
statement: Let $A$ specify the number of items and the counter region, let $kf$ assign a key to each item index, let $r$ be a natural number, and let $\mu'$ be a memory map from natural-number addresses to integers. For every natural number $t\le r$, the cell at address $A.cnt+t$ contains the number of indices $i<A.n$ whose key is less than $t$. For every natural number $t<A.nb$ with $r\le t$, the cell at address $A.cnt+(t+1)$ contains the number of indices $i<A.n$ whose key equals $t$.
